rule: `[[T alloc] init…]` is `T#alloc` plus `T#init…` (the init runs on a T) | **medium**: the callee is named statically (Type.m(), module.f(), an import, `self.m()` inherited from a base outside the scan, an external library type) but is not defined in the scan. | Call on a **computed receiver** (call result, index, literal, `super` when the superclass is not in the scan): `.member` — a leading dot means "receiver unknown".
notes: call_type convention used throughout this corpus: a callee that is a member of a type (`T#m`) or a receiver-qualified guess (`recv.m`, `.m`) is `method`; a C function (bare name) is `direct`. `[[Person alloc] initWithName:]` is `Person#alloc` plus `Person#initWithName:` (Decision 2026-10-29 ObjC). Person is in the scan but alloc/new are inherited from NSObject (outside the scan) → `Person#alloc` / `Person#new` medium (tier rule: `self.m()` inherited from a base outside the scan; C2: inherited from a base outside the scan). External classes: `NSMutableArray#alloc`, `NSMutableArray#init` (the init runs on an NSMutableArray), `NSString#stringWithUTF8String:` medium (external library type named statically). `list` is declared `NSMutableArray *` → `NSMutableArray#addObject:` medium. `[super init]`: the superclass NSObject is not in the scan → computed receiver `.init`, low. String literals `@"a"` are not calls.
